name: mlp_gpt2_124m
description: MLP layer sequencer: two matmuls with a requantize and rectify between them, over a two-bank activation buffer of 64 each

derivation.rule: the activation bank is one tile; the matmul and requantizer formats come from those blocks, so a change to either changes this one

ports.name: load_valid
ports.desc: write an input activation into bank zero

ports.name: depth1
ports.desc: reduction length of the first matmul

ports.name: scale1
ports.desc: requantizer scale for the first matmul

ports.name: shift1
ports.desc: requantizer shift for the first matmul

ports.name: scale2
ports.desc: requantizer scale for the second matmul

ports.name: shift2
ports.desc: requantizer shift for the second matmul

ports.name: w_addr
ports.desc: weight address, into the weight memory

ports.name: o_valid
ports.desc: a layer output is on o_data

behavior: load_valid writes input activations into bank zero in order.
start runs the first matmul over bank zero, requantizes each column with scale1 and shift1, rectifies it and writes it to bank one.
It then runs the second matmul over bank one, requantizes with scale2 and shift2, and emits each result on o_data.
The second matmul's reduction length is the first one's column count, because that is what the first matmul produced. Taking it from an input instead would let the two disagree.
The weight address continues across both matmuls, so the second matrix follows the first in memory.
